append.text: **Ps 96:3 *Ignis ante ipsum præcédet* → *Um fogo irá adiante dele*** — *præcédere* given *ir adiante de* (MS1932; προπορεύσεται) so that *preceder* stays free for the friendly *præveníre* as 87:14 proposes; see the new row *præcédere*. No reader remarked.
**Ps 96:2 *Nubes, et calígo in circúitu ejus* → *Nuvem e névoa escura estão ao seu redor*** — the place this row named; the same Greek (γνόφος). No reader remarked.
**Ps 96:2 *corréctio sedis ejus* → *a firmeza do seu trono*** (see the row *corréctio*).
Ps 96:2 *in circúitu ejus* → *ao seu redor* (75:12's form); 96:3 *inflammábit in circúitu* → *queimará ao redor* (no object, as 11:9).
Ps 96:4 *Illuxérunt fúlgura ejus orbi terræ* → *Os seus relâmpagos iluminaram o mundo* — 76:19a copied (*fúlgura / coruscatiónes* one Greek word, ἀστραπαί → *relâmpagos*, D15).

**Ps 96:5 *Montes, sicut cera fluxérunt a fácie Dómini* → *Os montes, como cera, escorreram à face do Senhor*** — the third wax verse, one with 57:9 and 67:3; *derreteram-se* (the Greek, MS1932) option. The Latinist (v1, minor) asked *diante da face*; held for 67:3, option.

**Ps 96:5 *a fácie Dómini* ×2 → *à face do Senhor*** — Ps 67's wax-and-face image, kept one. The second colon *a fácie Dómini omnis terra* keeps the Latin's ellipsis (*omnis terra* nominative; the Greek's genitive 'Lord of all the earth', DRB, refused): *à face do Senhor, toda a terra*. The ambiguity reader heard a verbless statement; the supplied verb (*escorreu*) is an option.
**Ps 96:7 *et qui gloriántur in simulácris suis* → *e os que se gloriam nos seus ídolos*** — the idolaters' boasting this row kept the verb for. No reader remarked on the verb.

Ps 96:7b *Adoráte eum, omnes Ángeli ejus* → *Adorai-o, todos os seus anjos* (Heb 1:6). Draft 1 had *Adorai-o, vós, todos …* (the 29:5 / 30:24 build); the stylist heard the *vós* as a stumble blurring the address — dropped: with the object *-o* expressed, the noun can only be the vocative.

**Ps 96:9 *nimis exaltátus es super omnes deos* → *sois muito exaltado sobre todos os deuses*** — *muito* as the settled 47:2 = 95:4 formula (D43). The stylist found *muito exaltado* weak and asked *exaltado muito acima de* (refused: *super … super* kept); *exaltado sem medida* (118:138) the option.

**Ps 96:11 *Lux orta est justo* → *A luz nasceu para o justo*** — the row, subject first as 84:12; *justo* singular kept (MS1932 pluralizes). The ambiguity reader heard dawn first, 'the Light was born' second — both in the Latin.
Ps 96:11 *et rectis corde lætítia* → *e a alegria para os retos de coração* — applied; the ambiguity reader listed *retos* as unknown (kept).

**Ps 96:12 *confitémini memóriæ sanctificatiónis ejus* → *dai graças à memória da sua santidade*** — 29:5b word for word, not 'with its own noun': the Greek of both is τῆς ἁγιωσύνης (checked in both parallels files), so D15's test merges *sanctificátio* here with *sánctitas*. The Latinist asked *santificação* twice (minor; the v2 gate conceded *santidade* is the sense) — held, option. 95:6 *in sanctificatióne ejus* is ἁγίασμα (sanctuary), another sense. The ambiguity reader heard a faint papal *Sua Santidade* (29:5 shares it).

**Ps 96:7 *Confundántur omnes, qui adórant sculptília* → *Sejam envergonhados todos os que …*** (34:4's jussive). The stylist found the periphrastic passive heavy in a long colon (+7) and asked *Envergonhem-se* — refused for the row, option (`confundantur`).
Ps 96:10 *custódit Dóminus ánimas sanctórum suórum* → *o Senhor guarda as almas dos seus santos*; the ambiguity reader heard canonized saints first again (kept).

Ps 96:1 *exsúltet terra: læténtur ínsulæ multæ* → *exulte a terra: alegrem-se as ilhas numerosas* (the stylist's order for *multæ*); 96:8 *Et exsultavérunt fíliæ Judæ* → *E as filhas de Judá exultaram* (subject first — *E ex-* clashed; 47:12a keeps verb first); 96:12 *Lætámini, justi, in Dómino* → *Alegrai-vos, ó justos, no Senhor*. The ambiguity reader listed *exulte* as unknown (kept).
Ps 96:10 *de manu peccatóris liberábit eos* → *da mão do pecador os livrará* (the Latin's order, no *e*; MS1932 *livrá-los-á* an option).
**Ps 96:1 opens *O Senhor reinou, exulte a terra* — the formula copied.** The ambiguity reader heard a finished past first ('the Lord reigned once'); kept, the Latin's perfect.
**Ps 96:12b copies the colon word for word** (*e dai graças à memória da sua santidade*): *sanctificatiónis* here and *sanctitátis* there are one Greek word (ἁγιωσύνη) — see the memória row.

terms: | præcédere | ir adiante de (*Um fogo irá adiante dele*) | open | Ps 96:3 (*Ignis ante ipsum præcédet*, προπορεύσεται; MS1932 *irá adiante dele*, DRB 'go before'). Chosen so that *preceder* stays free for the friendly *præveníre* (87:14 *vos precederá*, proposed in that row). **88:15 *Misericórdia et véritas præcédent fáciem tuam*** has the same Greek verb and should follow (*irão adiante da vossa face*). 84:14 *Justítia ante eum ambulábit* is the same Greek phrase with another Latin verb and keeps *andará diante dele*. *o precederá* is option 3 in Ps 96 (warned). No reader remarked. |

| corréctio (sedis) | firmeza (*justiça e juízo são a firmeza do seu trono*) | open | Ps 96:2 only in the psalter (grep); the Latin's calque of κατόρθωσις, 'a setting upright, establishment' (DRB 'establishment'). L&S has only 'amendment'; the cognate *correção* is heard as correcting the throne. *a base* (MS1932; the Hebrew's 'foundation', and 88:15's *præparátio*) and *o aprumo* options. The v2 Latinist (minor) wanted a noun of action, *estabelecimento* — refused, heard as a shop. |

| inflammáre (fire, persons as object) | queimar (*e queimará ao redor os seus inimigos*) | open | Ps 96:3 (φλογιεῖ). Draft 1 *abrasará* (MS1932) was unknown to the ambiguity reader and heard as *abraçará* ('will embrace'); *queimar* is DRB's 'burn'. 72:21 *inflammátum est cor meum → se inflamou* (the heart; another Greek) and 104:19 *elóquium Dómini inflammávit eum* decide by their own object. |

| sculptília / scúlptile | imagens esculpidas / imagem esculpida | working | Ps 77:58 (*com as suas imagens esculpidas*), 96:7 *qui adórant sculptília* → *os que adoram imagens esculpidas* (colon +7, accepted; *esculturas* heard as art). 105:19, 105:35, 105:38 to come (grep). The ambiguity reader heard pagan idols first, with a faint echo of polemic against church statues. |

| simulácrum | ídolo (*e os que se gloriam nos seus ídolos*) | open | Ps 96:7 (εἴδωλα; DRB 'idols'); 113:12 = 134:15 *Simulácra géntium* to come (grep). The cognate *simulacros* (MS1932) is bookish; the stylist asked it to avoid the proparoxytone close of *ídolos* — refused (rule 5). Kept apart from *sculptília → imagens esculpidas* (the two stand in one verse). |
